title: Cryptographic Diffusion Layer XOR Circuits: minimize straight-line XOR gate count
description: Sunstead pins OpenSSL's verbatim diffusion layer implementations (`openssl/openssl@d94024ff`, Apache-2.0) for AES `MixColumns` & `InvMixColumns` (NIST FIPS 197, 32×32 over GF(2)), SM4 round `L` & key-schedule `L'` (RFC 8998 / ISO 18033-3, 32×32 over GF(2)), ARIA involutory diffusion `A` (RFC 5794 / ISO 18033-3, 16×16 over GF(2)), and Camellia `P`-function (RFC 3713 / ISO 18033-3, 8×8 over GF(2)). `CryptoLinearXor/Spec.lean` formally proves GF(2)-linearity, exact equivalence to the OpenSSL C constructions, invertibility/involution, and the Fundamental Linearity Soundness Theorem lifting a single-pass basis-mask check to all 2^n inputs (2^32 = 4,294,967,296 inputs for 32-bit layers) in pure Lean 4.36.0 (no Mathlib). Six independent hill-climb tracks start from unoptimized row-by-row XOR trees and challenge contributors to minimize straight-line XOR gate count (known research frontiers: 92, 103, ~72–90, ~45–56, 36, 16).

tasks.title: AES MixColumns (32×32): minimize straight-line XOR gate count
tasks.description: Submit a straight-line XOR circuit implementing NIST FIPS 197 §5.1.3 / OpenSSL AES `MixColumns` (32×32 over GF(2), polynomial 0x11b, column [02, 03, 01, 01]) in `CryptoLinearXor/AesMixColumnsCircuit.lean` (`aesMixColumnsScore`, `aesMixColumnsGates`, `aesMixColumnsOutputs`). Seeded with a naive row-wise XOR tree (152 XORs; literature frontier: 92). The frozen Lean 4 kernel proof verifies well-formedness, XOR gate count, and exact equivalence on all 2^32 inputs via linearity soundness. Only strict improvements below the current record earn credit.
